To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
increased saturation of the sn- 2 position of phosphatidyl-choline in model biles reduces cholesterol crystallization.
the introduction of one double bond in the sn- 2 fatty acyl group of phosphatidyl choline increases the crystal observation time from 2 days to 14 days and reduces the crystal growth rate by 90%.
saturation of the biliary phosphatidyl-choline (PC) in the sn-1 and sn-2 position prolongs the crystal observation time, slows the crystal growth rate, and reduces the cholesterol crystal mass.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the phosphatidylinositol fatty acids in cholesterol crystallization in biliary lipid vesicles.
the molecular structure of bile and its effects on cholesterol crystallization.
the effects of varying the molecular structure of the PC sn-2 position on the cholesterol crystallizing properties of model biles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
increased saturation of the fatty acid in the sn- 2 position of phosphatidyl choline reduces cholesterol crystallization.

the increased saturation of the sn- 2 fatty acids in the phospholipids of model biles prolongs the crystal observation time, slows the crystal growth rate, reduces the crystal formation, and extends the cholesterol solubility.
increased saturation of the fatty acyl chain in the sn- 2 position of biliary phosphatidyl choline increases the cholesterol solubility and reduces crystallization in model human bile.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the molecular structure of the biliary phospholips is of major importance for the cholesterol crystallization processes.
the saturation of the biliary sn-2 fatty acids in the phospholipids has major effects on cholesterol crystallization in bile, and that these effects are reversed by desaturation of these fatty acids.
the saturation of the biliary phospholipopids is a key factor that controls the cholesterol crystallization in bile.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cholesterol crystallization in bile is affected by the saturation of the fatty acid in the sn- 2 position of the PC.
the saturation of the fatty acid in the sn-1 position of the biliary phospholipopids is not as important as the saturation in the sn- 2 position for the cholesterol crystallization in the biles.
saturation of the sn-1 and sn-2 fatty acids of phosphatidyl-choline is important in regulating the solubility and crystallization of cholesterol in biliary lipids.
